stories.notes: Story has zero acceptance criteria and null spec — no prior hand-curation. Live Preview is a complex, cross-platform CMS feature (GO, UP, MX) requiring real-time rendering and state sync. openspec needed to elaborate requirements and define ACs from scratch; speckit needed to harden testability, flag security concerns (XSS in preview rendering, iframe sandboxing), and identify edge cases. openspec runs first, then speckit reviews its output.

agentContributions.notes: Novel story — Live Preview does not exist in the codebase. The single attachment point is ContentstackProvider, which currently creates an immutable context from defaultContent and must be extended to subscribe to @contentstack/live-preview-utils for real-time updates. 236+ components depend on useContent which reads from this provider, so no downstream changes are needed if the provider itself is modified. ACs were empty; VCs derived from the title/description intent plus the fix-site analysis.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria, so all 12 ACs are original to speckit. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1 covers the core happy-path real-time update behavior. (2) AC-2 ensures graceful degradation — Live Preview must be opt-in and non-breaking. (3) AC-3 protects the 236+ downstream useContent consumers per openspec's analysis. (4) AC-4 addresses rapid-update race conditions. (5) AC-5 covers SSR/hydration consistency, critical for Next.js apps. (6) AC-6 prevents memory leaks on unmount. (7) AC-7 is a security gate — preview tokens must not leak to production. (8) AC-8 explicitly covers ContentstackLink since it was flagged in technicalNotes. (9) AC-9 ensures cross-site parity despite the file naming differences (ContentstackContext.tsx vs ContentstackContext.ts vs contentstackContext.tsx) noted in perCodeline. (10) AC-10 covers SDK initialization failure. (11) AC-11 covers nested/referenced content updates. (12) AC-12 ensures no end-user performance penalty. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I could not read the actual file contents of ContentstackContext, contentCard, ContentstackLink, or useContent — AC precision could improve with access to those files, particularly around the exact shape of the content object and how references are resolved.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Brownfield cross-codeline (GO/UP/MX) Live Preview story. All four manifest paths confirmed EXISTS with zero unresolved per-codeline paths. The two extension_variant matches (gotransit .ts→.tsx, metrolinx ContentstackContext.tsx→contentstackContext.tsx) are resolved and speckit's AC-9 explicitly addresses cross-site naming parity. Verification criteria are all observable: unchanged-field correctness, malformed-update resilience, non-preview correctness, post-exit correctness. Both agents delivered non-overlapping value — openspec identified the architectural attachment point (ContentstackProvider → 236+ useContent consumers, no downstream changes needed if provider is modified) and derived VCs; speckit authored 12 comprehensive ACs covering security (preview token leakage), race conditions, SSR/hydration consistency, memory leaks, SDK init failure, nested content, and cross-site parity. Empty acceptanceCriteria array is expected brownfield redaction — not flagged. File set is plausible: context provider, content interface, link component, and content hook are exactly the surfaces a Live Preview integration would touch. No concrete defect identified.
